subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs before they can run on inherited provider/model defaults?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the repair changes shipped cron activation defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, model-cost policy, and quota enforcement behavior that need maintainer intent.

options.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Require operator-visible approval or explicit activation for external/plugin recurring agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and define doctor/update migration behavior together.

options.title: Narrow model-cost warning first
options.body: Add warnings or blocking only when recurring jobs inherit expensive defaults, leaving activation and provenance to separate follow-up work.

options.title: Split and track only canonical sub-issues
options.body: Keep this issue as a cluster index while #71712, #14376, and #42475 own provenance, recurring guardrails, and budget enforcement independently.

recommendation.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible approval or explicit activation for external/plugin recurring agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and define doctor/update migration behavior together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron/plugin scheduling refactors and broad area history make this the strongest available owner for deciding the cross-boundary fix shape.
